newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian report slams New Zealand defence spending.
newsitem.headline: Australian report slams New Zealand defence spending.

text.p: Australia, in damage control over the loss of a top secret paper critical of the South Pacific, on Wednesday faced the leaking of another secret report which said New Zealand's defence spending was "inadequate".

The 39-page document -- marked 'AUSTEO', or Australian Eyes Only -- details a cabinet strategy of Australian ministers pressing the need for bigger military spending on their New Zealand counterparts at every opportunity.

It follows publication of a more detailed AUSTEO paper by Reuters last week, which contained a scathing assessment of South Pacific economies and the foibles and mismanagement of some leaders and ministers.
A major investigation has already been launched into the loss of the first AUSTEO document, regarded as one of the worst security breaches in several years.

Both documents were briefing papers for Treasurer Peter Costello for a summit of economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum in the tropical Australian resort town of Cairns earlier this month.
AUSTEO is one of Australia's highest security ratings.
The latest document outlines Australian concern at New Zealand's defence budget and Canberra's feeling that it carries an unfair share of the bilateral defence burden.
"Inadequate NZ defence funding might mean Australia was seen to be accepting a disproportionate share of the bilateral burden," the paper said.
The New Zealand briefing says that even the latest draft of Wellington's upcoming defence review would see long-term defence stalled below 1990/91 levels.

The paper urges Costello to lobby New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters -- labelled an opportunist and loose cannon in the first paper -- on the need for Wellington to take more responsibility for defence.

"Raising Australia's concerns with Winston Peters...will register this message with the cabinet member who holds the 'purse-strings' over competing NZ budget priorities -- especially social policy versus defence interests," it said.

The paper was one of several left on a table in a public area at the hotel where the economic ministers' summit was held. It was published on Wednesday by the Australian Associated Press news agency and a copy was obtained by Reuters.
The document is a series of briefing notes for Costello's bilateral talks with his 15 guests after the summit.
It outlines economic and trade issues, as well as the state of bilateral relations, for all 15 other forum countries.
Publication of the first AUSTEO document sparked an angry response in the South Pacific, with leaders attacking it as offensive, disrespectful and wrong.
Fiji Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has said Australian Prime Minister John Howard would be taken to task over the paper at the summit of forum leaders in the Cook Islands in September.
